findings.reason: the section would reimplement a landed, tested mechanism, so it should be deleted or rewritten around the one gap the existing hold does not cover.
findings.text: §1's "What changes" is existing code: `_identity_hold` holds the reading against `git_head._head_identity` (a stat-only read of `.git/HEAD`, the ref it names and `commondir`, with no git spawn) and `source_code_identity` (`reckon/checkout_trust.py:419`) re-derives with `git ls-tree`/`mktree` only when that reading moves; `tests/test_the_code_identity_is_read_only_when_head_moves.py` already proves the plan's four done-when cases, including "20 identity reads against an unmoved HEAD start git only on the first read" (`:113`) and "a commit outside the package moves the stamp and runs the reads" (`:241`), and `tests/test_a_commit_without_code_moves_no_identity.py:101` covers the third

findings.reason: the diagnosis is aimed at `_FollowerReloader.poll` and the wrong layer; the fix is to key the existing hold on the image commit the reloader already carries in `RECKON_FOLLOWER_IMAGE_COMMIT`, not to add a second key reader.
findings.text: the gap the existing hold really leaves is the reload-image path, which the plan never names: `stamp = _head_identity(source_root) if own_root else None` returns `None` outside git, and a follower re-exec'd from a published image has no `.git` (`materialize_committed_tree` extracts a `git archive` tarball at `reckon/checkout_trust.py:600-621`), so every tick of a reloaded follower spawns `git -C <image> ls-tree HEAD reckon skills` that fails and then falls through to `code_stamp`'s `rglob("*.py")` walk (`reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:729`) — which is the per-second cost the strace measured, and the one place the plan's new key machinery would still be needed

findings.reason: the change belongs inside the existing function (extend the stamp to cover the image case), which also collapses three write paths to one.
findings.text: §1's write paths span three modules for behaviour that is a single guarded dictionary lookup and one conditional already inside `source_code_identity`, so the plan's placement turns one deep function into a key reader in `checkout_trust`, a call site in `follower_reload` and an unchanged `follower_registration`, adding surface without depth

findings.reason: the item asks for exactly this justification, and here the honest change is an extension of the owner rather than a parallel path beside it.
findings.text: the plan's §1 places the identity key in the follower, which is a wrapper over `checkout_trust.source_code_identity` — the function that already resolves the source root, already holds the identity and already returns `IDENTITY_UNKNOWN` on a failed read — and never says why that function cannot be extended

findings.reason: landing §2 as written leaves two caches for one file that can disagree, and the plan must say which one goes.
findings.text: `_identity_catalogue` is already a stamp-keyed cache for the model catalogue (`@lru_cache(maxsize=8)` keyed on `_file_identity(path)` at `reckon/ledger.py:1170`), and `resolve_name` reads through it (`reckon/ledger.py:252`), so §2's "memo at the one read boundary" would be the second memo for this file; the plan does not name `_identity_catalogue` for retirement or say what becomes of it

findings.reason: the section should cite `file_memo.memoized` as the mechanism it extends and name `_identity_catalogue` as what it retires, which is the difference between a fix and a third memo.
findings.text: §2's stated requirement "callers receive a value they cannot mutate into the cache: either an immutable view, or a copy" is `reckon/file_memo.memoized` verbatim — `copy.deepcopy` on hand-out (`reckon/file_memo.py:406`) and `read_only_region` for a shared view (`:257`) — while the existing `_identity_catalogue` fails it: I confirmed on this checkout that `ledger._identity_catalogue(p, ledger._file_identity(p)) is ledger._identity_catalogue(...)` is True and a `__mutated__` key written into the first result is visible in the second, so the defect §2 identifies is real and its remedy is already owned here

findings.reason: both sections are about stat-keyed identity, so a section touching them should route through `signature_from_stat` rather than add a fifth spelling of the same tuple.
findings.text: census of the stat-identity helper §1 and §2 both need: `signature_from_stat` is the declared owner ("The one place the identity's fields and their order are written"), and the same tuple is re-derived at `reckon/git_head.py:46` `_file_identity` (mtime_ns, ino, size), `reckon/ledger.py:1170` `_file_identity` (mtime_ns, ctime_ns, size, ino), `reckon/crew/review_records.py:1308` `_stat_identity`, `reckon/crew/recovery_memo.py:108` `_file_identity`, `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1018`, `reckon/roadmap_snapshot.py:375`, `reckon/mcp_deadlines.py:215`, `reckon/serve.py:786`, `reckon/project_state.py:1174`, `reckon/_backends.py:2789`

findings.reason: with public_definitions at 2448 the rule is that every section names what it merges or retires; §1 retires nothing because it duplicates, and §2 leaves the duplicate it should absorb.
findings.text: the two sections add public surface and retire none: §1 leaves `FOLLOWER_FRESHNESS_SECONDS` and its per-tick `follower_code_stamp()` call in place while adding a key-read definition and a new test module; §2 adds a catalogue memo while leaving `ledger._identity_catalogue` and `lanes_declaring_model`'s direct uncached `flight.read_layer_file` call (`reckon/ledger.py:307`) in place

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §1 spreads a key-read, a hold and a re-derive across three modules (`checkout_trust.py`, `follower_reload.py`, `follower_registration.py`) when the whole mechanism is one bounded dict and one guard in `checkout_trust.source_code_identity`; §2 is sound on this item, since one memo at `flight.read_layer_file` is smaller than the callers it serves.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §1 duplicates `checkout_trust._identity_hold`, and §2 adds a second catalogue memo beside `ledger._identity_catalogue` without naming it for retirement, while `reckon/file_memo.py` owns stat-keyed parse memoisation for the repository.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 2448, cli_options 470, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 25; §1 adds a public key-read definition and a test module while identical definitions already exist, and §2 adds a memo without retiring `ledger._identity_catalogue`, so neither section names what it retires, merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan adds no reuse map, and the mechanism §1 proposes in full already exists at `reckon/checkout_trust.py:101` (`_identity_hold`, landed 33ad6f4bbe 2026-10-19) keyed on `reckon/git_head.py:82` `_head_identity`, with eight covering tests in `tests/test_the_code_identity_is_read_only_when_head_moves.py`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §1 would place the new key check in `follower_reload.py` beside `checkout_trust.source_code_identity`, a forwarding layer over machinery that is already the extension point it needs to be.
